title: The base model's scorecard, and the noise of measuring it
design_ref: Evaluation: scorecards and no-regression gates; the capability matrix (seed noise first)
purpose: Score the untrained model on every family's held-out set three times with different sampling seeds. The spread is the noise floor of a single evaluation; every difference reported later is read against it.

steps.display: python scorecard.py base-scorecard-s02   # mean reward over 100 held-out prompts x 4 samples; three sampling seeds

checks.description: no family sits at its floor or ceiling, so each has something to learn and something to lose (every score between 0.10 and 0.95)
checks.because: I tuned the tools and instruction families after a first look (the first versions scored 1.00 and 0.89), because a family at its ceiling cannot show transfer and one at its floor cannot show interference.

checks.description: a single evaluation is repeatable: no family's three sampling seeds differ by more than 0.03 (standard deviation)
checks.because: Each score is a mean over 400 sampled answers. The spread printed here is what the matrix of S03 and the gate of S09 treat as noise from sampling; the noise from training seeds is measured separately in S03.

checks.description: the answer lengths used to balance batches by tokens are the measured ones (each within 35% of the base model's mean)
checks.because: Balancing a batch by tokens (S06) needs each family's mean answer length. The constants in the code are these measurements; a family whose answers get much longer or shorter under training makes the balance drift, which S06 shows.
